thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A browser-based ROS2 development, simulation, teleoperation, navigation, manipulation and automation platform, supplemented by enterprise support and a Catalyst service that scopes, configures, validates, deploys and supports customers' first robot application. The company states that customers need the outcome addressed by its described product; precise quantified pain was not independently verified. Verified current scope: developer/test environment only; company-hosted DarbyTech case claims inspection deployment. Stated ambition: end-to-end workflow across assets. Public evidence supports responsibility for simulation/training; supports only partial/shared responsibility for models/policies, integration, commissioning/qualification and ongoing support/maintenance; does not establish responsibility for hardware, robot body, end effectors/tooling, remote operations and hardware financing/RaaS. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 2_first_party_deployment_claim; technical evidence: 3_vendor_documented. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 2_first_party_deployment_claim; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
